rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad had not read scripture before the Quran was revealed and still did not write, so opponents lacked a plausible human-source pretext.
rows.anchor: hâlâ elinle yazmazsın da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The falsifiers are unjust disbelievers pursuing falsehood or seeking a pretext to invalidate the message; fair-minded seekers would not doubt.
rows.anchor: o mubtıller, yani bâtıl peşinde giden, yahut ibtâle bahane arayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illiteracy is not a condition for miraculous eloquence, since other prophets were literate; it merely removes an excuse for hostile doubters.
rows.anchor: Çünkü i‘câz için ümmîlik şart değildir. Nitekim sâir peygamberler ümmî değillerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes فِي as attached to بَيِّنَاتٌ; this is contextually evident in the passage about removing doubt and avoids an ellipsis.
rows.anchor: haziften selâmet itibariyle de ercahtır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran consists of manifest divine signs and miracles, unmistakably clear in the hearts of people given knowledge and leaving no room for doubt.
rows.anchor: Yani Allah tarafından birer alâmet, parlak mucizeler olduğu ehl-i ilmin gönüllerinde ayan beyan açık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are those who know the truth but refuse to acknowledge it, especially the truth-rejecting part of the People of the Book who denied the Quran as a sign.
rows.anchor: hakkı tanımak istemeyen, zulmü âdet edinmiş zâlimler

words: لَوْلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَٰتٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents demand signs like Moses’ staff or Salih’s she-camel; God alone sends the Quran and any other miracle as He wills, while Muhammad is only a clear warner.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın asâsı, Sâlih’in nâkası gibi mucizeler indirilse ya!

words: أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed book, publicly recited and given to a prophet who had not read or written before, should itself suffice as the requested miracle.
rows.anchor: Daha yetişmedi mi onlara o başka âyet, başka mucize isteyenlere kâfi gelmedi mi daha mucize olmak üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is a great blessing and divine admonition for those who will believe, not for people persisting in stubbornness and prejudice.
rows.anchor: ve bir ilâhî ihtâr ve nasihat var

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its immediate context, the assurance that the Quran suffices answers the unjust people who had demanded additional signs.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetin siyâk u sibâkına nazaran

rows.speaker: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: A report says some Muslims brought Jewish teachings written on a shoulder blade; the Prophet called preferring others’ revelations over their own prophet’s a folly or misguidance, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem “bir kavmin kendi peygamberlerinin getirdiğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although that shoulder-blade incident can be related to the verse, Elmalılı rejects it as the occasion of revelation: the surrounding pronouns refer to sign-demanding opponents, not Muslims.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bunun sebeb-i nüzul olması âyetin altına ve üstüne muvâfık düşmüyor.

words: أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha rejected a gift from Abdullah b. Amir, mistaking him for Abdullah b. Amr, because he studied other books and she cited this verse; she accepted it once corrected.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki Abdullah b. Âmir b. Rükn Hazret-i Âişe radıyallahu anhâ’ya bir hediye takdim etmişti.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: When Hafsa read a written account of Joseph, the Prophet said that following Joseph instead of him while he lived among them would lead them astray; he was their share among prophets and they his share among peoples.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Hafsa radıyallahu anhâ da bir kürek üzerine Yusuf kıssasından bir yazı getirmiş, Hazret-i Peygamber’e okumuştu

rows.speaker: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: After Umar copied and brought him another book, the Prophet’s face changed; he said he was sent as both opener and seal, given concise comprehensive speech, and warned against reckless or confused people leading others astray.
rows.anchor: Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurdu ki: “Ben hem fâtih ve hem hâtim ba‘s olundum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mütehevvikler are people who rush into matters without reflection or people who are bewildered.
rows.anchor: reviyyetsiz her işe dalanlar yahut mütehayyirler demektir

none: Translation only, followed by a bare heading for the next surah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers the apparent meaning of ribā as familiar interest or usury, rather than a figurative sense.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bundan murad, mâruf olan ribâ, yani faiz olduğunu söylemişlerdir ki zâhir olan da budur.

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that the verse concerned the usury of Thaqif; since Thaqif and Quraysh practiced usury, it censured interest before its later prohibition.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Süddî bu âyetin Sakīf’in ribâsı hakkında nâzil olduğunu rivayet eylemiştir.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Many exegetes, on a meaning transmitted from Ibn Abbas, take ribā figuratively as gifts given while expecting a greater return; the comparison censures such gifts like usury and more strongly implies usury’s prohibition.
rows.anchor: fazla hediyeler, atıyyeler olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır ki bu mâna İbn Abbas’tan mervîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the gift interpretation, expecting extra repayment earns no reward, though the gift itself is not sinful; actual usury likewise has no reward with God.
rows.anchor: Gerçi bu günah değildir, fakat sevâbı da yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alms given seeking God’s pleasure are the true multipliers, and their reward is multiplied as in the grain yielding seven ears with a hundred grains each.
rows.anchor: Allah yüzünü, Allah rızâsını murad ederek verdiğiniz zekât ise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To know God, one should not speculate over the divine essence through competing philosophies but reflect on God’s clear acts, effects, blessings, and favors.
rows.anchor: Dîn-i tevhid hakkındaki bu emirlerden ve bu beyânâttan sonra zât ve sıfât-ı ilâhiye hakkında türlü felsefelerle ihtilâfa düşülmeksizin Allah’ı tanıtmak için

words: خَلَقَكُمْ ثُمَّ رَزَقَكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creation, provision, death, and resurrection identify Him through acts that are evident to human beings.
rows.anchor: Şüphesiz ki sizi yaratan var, işte O sizi yaratandır.

words: هَلْ مِن شُرَكَآئِكُم مَّن يَفْعَلُ مِن ذَٰلِكُم مِّن شَىْءٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: None of the partners can do any of these acts, so God is exalted and utterly remote from their association with Him.
rows.anchor: Hiç sizin şerîklerinizden bunlardan bir şey yapan var mı? Yok olduğu şüphesiz.

words: فَلَا تَكُن فِى مِرْيَةٍۢ مِّن لِّقَآئِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God gave Moses a book, He now gives one to Muhammad as announced at the surah’s opening; Muhammad should have no doubt about receiving it.
rows.anchor: Şimdi sen onun likāsından şüphede olma yani vaktiyle Mûsâ’ya verdiğimiz gibi şimdi de sûrenin başında beyan olunduğu üzere sana kitap veriyoruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frequent remembrance covers all times and all forms of fitting remembrance, including sanctifying, magnifying, declaring God’s oneness, and praising Him.
rows.anchor: çok zikir vakitlere gālib ve takdis, temcid, tehlil, tahmid gibi Allah’a lâyık zikrin envâ‘ına şâmil olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse singles out glorification among forms of remembrance and morning and evening among times because tasbih is central and those are well-known times.
rows.anchor: Bununla beraber envâ‘-ı zikr içinde tesbihin, evkāt içinde sabah ile akşamın bilhassa ehemmiyet ve faziletine işaret için de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the corresponding Turkish expression, morning and evening can figuratively mean continuing throughout all times.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh “sabah”, “akşam” tâbirleri Türkçemizde olduğu gibi Arapça’da da ta‘mîm-i evkāt ile devamdan kinaye de olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both remembrance and tasbih also include prayer.
rows.anchor: Kezâlik “zikr” ü “tesbih” namaza dahi şâmildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted David a special, extraordinary divine favor and miracle, beyond ordinary gifts and surpassing what earlier prophets had received; David was especially devoted in turning to God.
rows.anchor: yani alelâde değil, azamet-i ilâhiyeyi ayrıca bir husûsiyetle ifade eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David’s beautiful voice and glorious delivery made mountains and birds join his morning and evening glorification; this miraculous favor is explained through the parallel accounts in 21:79 and 38:18–19.
rows.anchor: onun sesine bütün dağlar ve kuşlar iştirak eder, çınlar öterlerdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful melody is not categorically blameworthy in Islam: licentious melodies are censured, whereas reciting the Quran with measured pacing and an improved voice is commanded.
rows.anchor: Bu güzel sanatı İslâm’da sûret-i mutlakada mezmum zannedenler olmuştur. Fakat bilmek lâzım gelir ki mezmum olan lühûn-ı fısktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Music directly affects the body and nerves through vibrating air; it gains spiritual value only when it helps the meaning of words reach the soul.
rows.anchor: Tegannî ancak bir kelimenin, bir kelâmın mânasını rûha duyurmaya hizmet etmesi itibariyledir ki rûhânî bir kıymet alabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Licentious singers seek bodily excitement through sensual themes and meaningless sounds that extinguish spiritual awareness, while religion seeks a beautiful, meaningful, sacred, conscious life.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i fısk, hep şehevânî mevzularla cismânî heyecan aradığı için mânayı öldürerek sade a‘sâba basan kuru nağmelerle cismânî tesir arar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran recitation should beautify the voice while preserving pronunciation, eloquence, and the meaning’s rhetorical subtleties; the prophetic expression lühûn-ı Arab is defined in recitation science through tajwid.
rows.anchor: elfâzın tecvîdini, fesâhatini bozmayarak, mânasını belâgatinin incelikleriyle duyurarak

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: The Prophet praised a beautiful Quran reciter by saying that he had been given one of David’s psaltery-like melodies.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Kur’ân’ı güzel okuyan hakkında “Âl-i Dâvûd’un mezâmîrinden bir mizmar verilmiştir” diye sitâyiş buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative Ya mountains treats them like rational beings, and the birds are coordinated in their place to express the meaning eloquently.
rows.anchor: zevi’l-ukūl gibi gösterilerek يَٰجِبَالُ diye nidâ, وَٱلطَّيْرَ onun mahalline atfedilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes explain that iron softened in David’s hand like wax, so he could shape it at will without first heating or hammering it.
rows.anchor: Kızdırmaya, dövmeye muhtaç olmaksızın elinde balmumu gibi dilediği surete koyuverdi.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says this should not be deemed impossible by God’s power: iron already softens and melts in fire, so no rational person should find it beyond divine power.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Allah’ın kudretinden bunu istib‘âd etmemelidir. Çünkü görülüyor, ateşte öyle yumuşuyor ve öyle münhal oluyor ki yazı yazılan mürekkeb hâline geliyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the softening as discovery of extracting and melting iron with fire and tools; Elmalılı rejects this reading as arising from weak faith and distrust of divine power.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bu doğru değildir. İtikādının zaafı ve Allah’ın kudretine ‘adem-i i‘timâdı onu bu fikre sevketmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Still, the verse may allow that iron smelting was already known but David developed it into the fine craft of shaping iron thinly enough to make armor.
rows.anchor: Demirin keşfi ve izâbesi daha eski olsa gerektir. Fakat onu mum gibi dilediği şekle koyarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel in 21:80 says armor-making protects people from battle; its address to you is directed to Muhammad’s community, suggesting the craft was passed on.
rows.anchor: buyurulmuştu ki bundan bu sanatın ahlâfa da yâdigâr kaldığı anlaşılıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David is told to make ample, full armor and measure its interlinking and form carefully, applying skill to its design.
rows.anchor: ve serdinde takdir sahibi ol yani

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wisdom in praising armor is that it protects human life from killing; makers of defensive protection benefit humanity more than makers of attack weapons and serve peace.
rows.anchor: bu sanatta لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ buyurulduğu üzere indallah mükerrem olan âdemiyeti katilden muhafaza ile rûhu vikāye vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the plural command as addressed to David and his household; Elmalılı instead prefers it as an appended lesson addressing Muhammad’s community, as in 21:80.
rows.anchor: bu cümle zamirinin Dâvûd ile beraber maiyyetindeki ehline râci‘olduğunu söylemişler ise de biz bunun لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ gibi kıssanın bir ibreti olmak üzere ümmet-i Muhammed’e hitap ile bir tezyil olduğu kanaatindeyiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees whatever people do and will reward them accordingly.
rows.anchor: çünkü ben ne yapacağınızı gözetiyorum, her ne yaparsanız görürüm yani ona göre mükâfâtını veririm.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon was given one special wind, not command over all winds; all canonical readings have singular al-rīḥ, never plural al-riyāḥ, and the wind could be directed to travel.
rows.anchor: bütün kıraatlerde bu الرّ۪يحَ müfred okunmuş, hiçbirinde ال ِّرياح okunmamıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind traveled one month’s distance in the morning and another in the evening, calculated as 900 kilometers each way and 1,800 round trip; the pronoun refers to the wind, emphasizing its speed.
rows.anchor: gidişi dokuz yüz kilometre, gelişi de dokuz yüz kilometre olarak bin sekiz yüz kilometre kat‘eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı leaves open whether Solomon traveled with the wind like a balloon or an airplane, saying God knows.
rows.anchor: Süleyman aleyhisselâm bununla balon gibi mi yoksa tayyâre gibi mi giderdi orasını Allah bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A closing Turkish couplet says Solomon’s throne once traveled through the air and that winds now blow where that sovereignty stood.
rows.anchor: Seyretti hevâ üzre denir taht-ı Süleyman Ol saltanatın yeller eser şimdi yerinde
